s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm
salient_findings: Severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm
ST-segment elevation and depression on ECG
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 50s
Presented with 1 hour of acute, severe precordial chest pain
Chest pain radiated to the left arm
Accompanied by sweating and nausea
Similar chest pain occurred 6 hours prior and resolved spontaneously
Medical history of hypertension treated with reserpine
Vital signs: blood pressure 170/109 mm Hg, heart rate 87 beats per minute
Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL
ECG showed upsloping ST-segment depression and ST-segment elevation
Coronary angiography revealed 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
Echocardiography showed hypomotility in the anterior wall and left ventricular ejection fraction: 57%

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin level and ECG changes consistent with myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: Unstable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Recent chest pain at rest and ECG changes consistent with ischemia

shortlist.label: Variant angina
shortlist.why_kept: ECG changes consistent with coronary artery spasm

shortlist.label: Coronary artery spasm
shortlist.why_kept: ECG changes and coronary angiography results suggest possible spasm

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG changes and left ventricular ejection fraction suggest possible stress-induced cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea, along with elevated serum troponin I level (1.159 ng/mL) and ECG changes, strongly supports the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction. The coronary angiography revealing 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery further confirms this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: The presence of elevated troponin levels and ECG changes indicating myocardial damage makes unstable angina less likely

rejected.label: Variant angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG changes are not consistent with variant angina, which typically presents with chest pain at rest and transient ST-segment elevation

rejected.label: Coronary artery spasm
rejected.why: While coronary artery spasm could cause chest pain, the presence of elevated troponin levels and significant coronary stenosis makes it less likely

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and diagnostic findings, including the presence of significant coronary stenosis, do not support a diagnosis of takotsubo cardiomyopathy
